_about:
HAND-DRAWN ADMIN AREAS — places a regulation describes as a POLYGON.

A regulation that says 'the area bounded by a line from a sign at X to a sign on the opposite bank, thence ...' is not a reach between two cut-points. Binding it as one closes the full width of the river instead of the area the signs enclose. These are the polygons, digitised.

Each feature becomes one admin area, exactly like a park or a WMA: an `areas.json` entry selects this layer with `cut: true`, so `area_splits` cuts every stream at first-enter/last-exit of the ring, the inside reaches are stamped `in_areas`, and `export_admin` draws the polygon into the tiles. Nothing new is needed in `load_area_polys` — the layer reaches the gpkg the same way `land_access` does.

PROPERTIES
  id     stable key; the area id is minted as area:{kind}:{slug(name)}
  name   what the area is called; this is what the area id slugs from, so do not reword it casually
  kind   the area family (sign_zone — an area bounded by fishing boundary signs)

THESE ARE PLACES, NOT RULES. A ring says where; what is forbidden inside it belongs to each
rule that binds to it, and they differ — the Kispiox zone carries a provincial no-angling-from-
a-vessel rule AND DFO salmon rules. Naming the area after one rule type would make the other
rules look like closures. Bind with an extent (`within_area`), exactly as you would to a split.
  cuts   the registry item this ring is cutting — the link the tile carries so a viewer can get from the polygon back to the water
  note   why the polygon exists and which vertices are authority vs estimate

STATUS: both rings reviewed by the curator against OSM + the FWA blue lines, 2026-09-21. Neither regulation states a distance and no source records the sign positions, so these rings are a reading, not a survey — but they are a curator's reading, which is the authority this repo uses everywhere else. Rings are EPSG:4326, lon/lat, first point repeated to close.

properties.name: Skeena River — Kispiox confluence sign zone
properties.note: REVIEWED 2026-09-21. The zone spans the Kispiox mouth, which sits INSIDE the ring — so the Skeena crosses the boundary twice (enter, exit) and the Kispiox once (it ends at the confluence). 14.2 ha. FOUR rules bind here and they are NOT all closures: the province prohibits angling from a vessel, DFO carries salmon rules in three wordings (4 / 3 / three triangular signs; one zone, see pipeline/docs/GOTCHAS.md). The ring is the PLACE; what is forbidden inside it is each rule's own business.

properties.name: Fraser River — Landstrom Bar sign zone
properties.note: REVIEWED 2026-09-21. 11.5 ha on the north side of the Fraser; the mainstem crosses the boundary twice. The regulation reads: sign at the E end of Landstrom Bar (Scale Bar) -> a sign on the opposite bank -> a sign at the S end of Croft Island -> a sign on the nearest bank westerly -> thence FOLLOWING THE BANK back to the point of commencement. The closing edge is a straight line here, not a traced bank; that changes the drawn shape, never the cut, which uses first-enter/last-exit only.
